# Noya CLI

Use the `noya` CLI to interact with Noya's data + chain + prediction-market APIs from the command line. The CLI wraps the Noya SDK; every command maps 1:1 to an SDK method.

## When to use this skill

- Reading wallet identity and signing arbitrary messages / transactions / typed data → `noya account …`
- Executing on-chain transactions (ERC-20 transfers, Compound/Morpho lending, swaps, approvals) → `noya chain …`
- Querying crypto prices, market data, news, or on-chain analytics → `noya data …`
- Reading portfolio holdings, DCA strategies, and positions → `noya portfolio …`
- Searching, reading, or trading on prediction markets (Polymarket, Kalshi, Limitless, …) → `noya predict …`
- Reading or interacting with agent conversation threads → `noya threads …`

## Installation

Install the `noya` CLI globally:

```bash
npm install -g @noya-ai/cli       # or: pnpm add -g @noya-ai/cli
```

Or run a single command without installing via `npx`:

```bash
npx @noya-ai/cli data coingecko price --token-ids bitcoin
```

Verify the install:

```bash
noya --version
```

## Authentication

Set one of:

```bash
export NOYA_API_KEY=noya_...     # generate at https://agent.noya.ai/api-keys
noya auth login                  # interactive OAuth (browser-based)
```

Anonymous mode (no creds) works for `noya data …` reads. Chain operations, prediction-market trading, and account/wallet operations require authentication.

## Quick examples

```bash
# Crypto price data
noya data coingecko price --token-ids bitcoin,ethereum

# Search prediction markets across every venue
noya predict search-markets --query "election"

# ERC-20 transfer (requires signer)
noya chain erc20 transfer --chain-id 8453 \
  --contract-address 0x... --destination 0x... --amount 100000000

# Wallet identity
noya account address
```

## Output handling

Every command prints its result as JSON to stdout. Pipe through `jq` to filter:

```bash
noya data coingecko price --token-ids bitcoin | jq '.bitcoin.usd'
```

Errors (auth failures, validation errors, network errors) print to stderr and exit non-zero. Always check exit code before parsing stdout.
